name: France 2018 World Cup
scopeNote: France at the Russia 2018 finals only, 16 June 2018 (v Australia, 2-1; date from FIFA article of 16 June) to 15 July 2018 (final v Croatia, 4-2, Moscow; FFF). Qualifying and the 2018 build-up are excluded, as is any other period under Deschamps. Sources call the style pragmatic, compact and counter-attacking (low/mid block, 4-2-3-1 attacking, 4-4-1-1 out of possession per Training Ground Guru/FIFA TSG); the popular label 'defensive' was rejected by Deschamps in a 2019 interview but is a press label. Many dates are tournament-level only ('2018') where the page does not give a match.
openQuestions: Zonal vs man-marking at set pieces for France 2018: no source read states it; only 'On a modifié un ou deux placements' (Deschamps, JDD). The SI line on 'tight man marking' is about Uruguay in open play.

Possession: Training Ground Guru says 48% (20th), LiveSoccerTV says 49% (19th), theScore says 18th, StatsBomb says 17th in passes per game. SI says France 'dominated possession' v Uruguay. Rankings differ by source.
Set-piece goal count: theScore says 6 of 14 goals from dead balls, a coaching summary seen in search says 5 of 14 (not mined).
Average squad age about 26 only seen in a search summary (unverified). FIFA says no outfield player over 27 in the Australia XI; Irish Times says all new players aged 25 or under except Nzonzi (29).
Matuidi on the left: theScore says field on the left wing; Irish Times says Griezmann started on the left v Belgium (Matuidi was not in that XI). Role varied by match.
Pavard was a right-back, Hernandez left-back; Umtiti and Varane centre-backs; Lloris-specific evidence not found beyond captaincy.
Benzema omission: sources say Deschamps excluded him; 'ruled himself out' claim relates to 2022 and is not used. Rabiot refused the standby list (Yahoo).

statedView.quote: The teams that had the highest level of possession, the highest level of control, were all punished by fast forwards. That is football. If you know how to defend well, you are guaranteed to have two or three opportunities on the counter-attack or on a set piece.
We had to defend deep, very deep at times because Belgium have technical quality. The idea was not to give them space because they've rolled over everyone (in reaching the semifinals), even Brazil.
They left them to pass backwards, to defenders who have low technical quality. The idea was to not give them space because they are a team that can be like lightning rods.
Adrien's performances with France are not at the same level as those he delivered with PSG this season.
On a modifié un ou deux placements. Pareil offensivement.
Contre l'Uruguay, on a cherché cet axe dans lequel ils mettaient leurs trois meilleurs joueurs de tête. [...] On s'est adaptés.
The most important choices are made when we choose the 23 players. You need to choose the men so you can build up a group that can go as far as possible.

confidence.reason: Good agreement across many 2018-dated sources (FIFA TSG data via Training Ground Guru, FA, Irish Times/Guardian, theScore, JDD interview), but few tier A tactical studies could be read (StatsBomb page truncated, Zonal Marking/Coaches' Voice not found); marking scheme and squad age undocumented.
